topic: Lambda Capture Value for Shared Future Handles
explanation: When launching multiple threads that rely on a shared event signal provided by a `std::shared_future`, the future handle must be captured by value (`[ sf ]`) in the worker lambda. Although the underlying shared state accessed by the future is thread-safe, the future object (the handle) itself is a local variable. Capturing by reference (`[&sf]`) would result in a data race if multiple threads accessed the local `sf` simultaneously, or if the local `sf` went out of scope prematurely. Capturing by value ensures each thread receives its own independent copy of the handle, thereby eliminating races on the handle object while still pointing to the single, shared state.
keywords: shared_future lambda capture, capture by value shared_future, future handle thread safety
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
